name: Hybrid model

subjectOf.text: The basic VC DAO model mixes fungible cryptocurrency investment with minted non fungible reputation, and this duality prevents the full benefits that are generated when non fungible reputation is staked alone on deals.
subjectOf.abstract: Rather, the VC DAO GP invests both fungible cryptocurrency from a pool as well as non-fungible and minted reputation on the portfolio companies. This duality does not allow for the full benefits that are generated if non-fungible reputation is staked alone on the deals.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614
scope_conditions: early phase VC DAO models that combine capital and reputation staking

subjectOf.text: Because of significant path dependencies in the capital formation and capital allocation processes of existing venture capital models, the ideal typical reputation based capital allocation model is less likely to be created in the short term.
subjectOf.abstract: because of significant path dependencies in the capital formation and capital allocation process with existing venture capital models, the above illustrated ideal-typical reputation-based capital allocation model in Figure 1 is less likely to be created in the short term.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614

subjectOf.text: In the hybrid VC DAO model eighty percent of returns are allocated to investors pro rata as ROI and twenty percent of returns are allocated to the reputation salary pool.
subjectOf.abstract: 80% of returns are allocated to investors pro rata as ROI. 20% of returns are allocated to the reputation salary pool.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614
scope_conditions: the hybrid VC DAO model with a traditional legal structure

subjectOf.text: The hybrid smart contracting model is defective because VCs are partially incentivized to fund and stake only the best deals while staking on less optimal deals that the market mostly funds, which undermines their long term reputation accumulation.
subjectOf.abstract: The problem with this model is that VCs are incentivized partially to fund and stake only on the best deals and stake on the less optimal deals that are mostly funded by the market. This undermines their long-term reputation accumulation
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614
scope_conditions: models where VCs can stake reputation without proportionate capital commitment

subjectOf.text: The hybrid model falls short of full community co-governance because it relies on a select group of experts for data validation and therefore may not capture the diverse perspectives and expertise of the broader community.
subjectOf.abstract: This is a significant step beyond the hybrid approach, which, while incorporating community input, primarily relies on a select group of experts for data validation and may not fully capture the diverse perspectives and expertise of a broader community.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4796714
scope_conditions: applies to the hybrid of community governance and decentralized data validation
concerns representativeness of the validating group
